parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national entry screening, passport marker rules, federal facility exclusion and federal custody are documented, severe and traveller-facing, and are not cancelled by the state layer. The state layer is strongly protective on its own matters: gender identity anti-discrimination since 1993, hate-crime coverage, abolished trans panic defence, a shield against out-of-state process, X marker on IDs, covered care and a conversion-therapy ban. The only custody placement harm is a dated 2012 case with no documented current rule. Street violence is not documented. Net: materially below a protective-state-only profile, above a national-exposure-only profile.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable directs refusal where documents or other evidence cast doubt on sex, and a permanent fraud-ground ineligibility finding is possible. Foreign ministry stopped processing non-matching markers; Supreme Court allowed restrictions in effect. Travellers report passports blocked and stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Limited: fraud finding requires all four elements, with limited waiver options; litigation pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal occurs before the state layer applies; state ID openness does not affect national passport or visa adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. State custody: 2012 placement of a trans woman in a men's facility, with a later hormone remedy only after petition. No current state custody data.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Petition process led to hormone regimen in the 2012 case; state shield and anti-discrimination law cover state-level conduct.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally faces national custody rules and the abuse record; a state-held visitor faces the dated birth-sex placement precedent, with no documented change.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities. National prisons adopted a conversion-style policy from 2026, and the corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodation coverage of gender identity; state facility restriction not documented for this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National government-building exclusion operates regardless of state protections; state facility status uncertain.

care_services.exposure: Subpoenas by national justice department for records of hospital patients under 19; proposed national rules would bar public reimbursement for under-18 care; national youth crisis services shut down.
care_services.protection: State health law covers transgender-related care, bars insurer exclusion, and shields providers and families from out-of-state process over legal care.
care_services.interaction: State protection does not bind federal subpoenas or national reimbursement rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralisation; reward system references 'radical gender ideology'. Advocates compare actions to early genocide.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State law explicitly protective; state documents treat gender-affirming care as lawful public policy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing is federal and sits above state protections.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition of minors. National health-records subpoenas cover under-19s. Athlete policy litigation is unresolved.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield protects families travelling for care from out-of-state subpoenas, warrants and custody orders. Conversion therapy banned for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family protection stops at state authority; federal school and records actions still reach a travelling child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence figure in the dossier. State hate-crime and discrimination enforcement data not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender identity covered in hate-crime law since 1993; trans panic defence abolished in 2024; discrimination law covers public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protections are state-level; national bias-crime statistics are not state-specific.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National passport, facility and care measures are in active litigation; several orders blocked. Outcome of state athlete-policy challenge and conversion-ban scope unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented state protections and court-based remedies for state-level matters; shield law text documented, with no reported application.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work at state level; national remedies are pending and unreliable for visitors in the interim.

anchor_checks.comparison: The 0.25-C case combines birth-sex housing with a criminal cross-dressing statute and frequent assaults in custody. This case has no criminal presentation statute and state protections, but shares national facility exclusion and documented birth-sex custody harm. Its state layer is stronger, so it sits above 0.25.

0.35-A has universal border exclusion with no effective appeal and no state shield. This case shares document-based entry refusal and national exclusion but has operating state protections and a shield law. It is higher than 0.35-A.

0.55-B has secondary screening and refusal of entry with no operative remedy. This case shares the entry-document exposure and federal custody abuse, but has state anti-discrimination, hate-crime and care protections. Comparable on entry, higher on the state layer, with federal custody harm keeping it near 0.55.

0.65-E has working appeals, barred detention and courteous officials at the border. This case lacks an operating remedy for national entry refusals and documents federal custody abuse without reform. It sits below 0.65 despite the strong state layer.

0.85-C has health-care access guaranteed nationally, with enforced remedies, and no federal custody exposure. This case has national subpoenas, proposed insurance bars and federal custody harm, so it is well below 0.85.

parsed.synthesis: National entry-document refusal, federal facility exclusion, national custody abuse and federal subpoenas of youth records are universal or severe exposures that the state layer cannot cancel. The state layer materially reduces exposure to state police, state care, state courts and hate crimes, and shields families from out-of-state process. The only state custody harm is dated (2012) with no documented change. The rating sits in the middle of the Elevated band: state protections are substantial, but national tier-one exposures and unremedied federal custody abuse hold the score down.
